title: Riff-Diff: computational enzyme design by catalytic motif scaffolding
summary: Riff-Diff places catalytic motifs around an active centre and uses RFdiffusion to generate the full protein; 35 tested sequences yielded active enzymes for several reaction types, reported as significantly faster than earlier computational designs. Angstrom-level accuracy was checked against experimentally determined high-resolution structures, and almost all designs kept their fold up to about 90 degrees Celsius. Figures come from university press coverage; the Nature paper itself was not read directly.
organization: TU Graz; and University of Graz (Oberdorfer group)

evidence.tested: 35 tested sequences were reported to yield active enzymes for several reaction types, with speed compared with earlier computer-aided designs and thermal stability up to about 90 degrees Celsius.
evidence.unknown: The page lists no limitations and does not say how many of the 35 sequences were active.
evidence.ai_role: RFdiffusion, a generative model, generated the complete protein structure from positioned catalytic motifs; other models refined the scaffold.
